title: Maximum Number of Balls in a Box
summary: In a ball factory where balls are numbered from lowLimit to highLimit, place each ball in a box whose number is determined by the sum of the digits of the ball's number.
statement: In a ball factory where balls are numbered from lowLimit to highLimit, place each ball in a box whose number is determined by the sum of the digits of the ball's number. For example, a ball numbered 321 goes into box number 6, and a ball numbered 10 goes into box number 1. Given the range of ball numbers, determine the maximum number of balls that end up in any single box.
constraints: Put every integer in the inclusive range into the box numbered by its decimal digit sum.
Return the largest number of balls in any box.
hints: Only a number’s digit sum determines its box.
Scan the inclusive interval and count each digit sum.
Compute the decimal digit sum, increment its frequency, then return the maximum frequency.
Every ball is assigned exactly once and the largest frequency is precisely the fullest box.
editorial: Every ball is assigned exactly once and the largest frequency is precisely the fullest box.

tests.explanation: Box one receives balls 1 and 10, so the maximum is two.
Digit-sum boxes five and six each receive two balls, and no box receives more.
